equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests at book (Reiss 25.7%, Joules, FatFace minorities)
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 AR consolidated statement of changes in equity, NCI column at 31 Jan 2026. Flows are 100% consolidated, so NCI is deducted once here.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 guidance (Q2 trading statement, 5 Aug 2026): Total Group sales +6.6%, re-based for the FY2026 53rd week to +4.6% on statutory revenue; fades to 2.5% by year 7. Historical CAGRs are not usable as a forward anchor: the 5-year base is the COVID year FY2021, the 3-year window includes consolidation of Reiss/Joules/FatFace and the 53rd week, and equity CAGR is distorted by GBP2.4bn of buybacks, B-share returns and the IFRS 16 transition.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 15.2% vs revenue 11.1% and EPS 9.3% diverge by more than 30%; 5yr equity 21.9% vs revenue 14.3%. Equity is distorted by the FY2021 COVID trough and heavy capital returns; it is NOT the selected rate.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - lease principal - lease interest; pre-IFRS16 years FY2017-19 are reported FCF - SBC only, since leases were already in EBITDA): FY2017 525.6, FY2018 496.9, FY2019 511.9, FY2020 549.3, FY2021 ~417, FY2022 462.5, FY2023 324.0, FY2024 697.4, FY2025 723.1, FY2026 795.9. The owner-FCF 5yr CAGR (13.8%) is ABOVE the reported FCF CAGR (9.9%) because lease cash (~GBP215-225m) has been flat in pounds while revenue nearly doubled -- the lease charge has fallen from 6.6% to 3.2% of revenue. The 3yr figure (34.9%) is off the FY2023 post-COVID inventory-rebuild trough and is not representative. SBC has grown faster than revenue (0.32% of revenue in FY2017 to 0.62% in FY2026), consistent with a rising share price inflating the IFRS 2 grant value, but remains small.

scenario_narratives.base: Next delivers the raised FY2027 guidance and then grows at 2.5-4% as International online, LABEL and WOBL offset a shrinking store estate; EBITDA margin holds at 23.4-23.8% with the lease charge drifting lower; capex normalises after the E3 warehouse programme. Value accrues through ~GBP0.8-1.2bn a year of owner FCF, largely returned to shareholders.
scenario_narratives.bull: International online keeps compounding at 15-20%, marketing ROI holds, Total Platform and WOBL scale at high ROCE, and operating leverage takes EBITDA margin to 25%. The company continues to beat and raise; Equal Pay is finally closed.
scenario_narratives.bear: Growth stalls in FY2028-29 as one-off tailwinds annualise, Shein takes UK online share, and UK consumer weakness plus a lost Equal Pay appeal compress margins to 21% while E3 capex is still being spent. The business remains solidly profitable and investment grade -- this is a de-rating, not a solvency, case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Next is a mature, exceptionally well-run UK retailer whose value is a stream of owner free cash flow after SBC and after the full cash cost of its leases, discounted at a GBP-built 9% WACC and capitalised at no more than 15x. The flows are consolidated and unlevered; ex-lease net debt and the minority interests are deducted once in the bridge. The market prices Next at ~18x forward EPS, above management's own 8% ERR buyback ceiling of GBP135; the DCF asks what growth and margin path that multiple requires.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal multiple: at a 9% WACC and 2% growth the Gordon value is near the 15x cap, so the result is sensitive to whether a mature UK retailer deserves 15x owner FCF in perpetuity.
Lease charge: treating leases as an operating cost deducts ~GBP220m a year; if the store estate shrinks faster than modelled the charge falls and value rises (and vice versa).
International marketing ROI: management says returns could fall from GBP1.75-2.08 to ~GBP1.01 per GBP1 spent if fixed-cost leverage is lost -- the single biggest swing in the growth path.
Equal Pay: a successful claimant appeal would add a structural store wage cost not in the base case.

Share count anchor: Jan 2026 count (116.9m) and Jan 2026 net debt are used as a pair; GBP355m+ of FY2027 buybacks have since reduced the count ~2.3% and raised net debt by a similar amount -- value-neutral in aggregate but the per-share split will move at the next balance sheet.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 11,695-16,175p
data_sources.financials: NXT.L_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (FY2017-FY2026 annual, H1 FY2017-H1 FY2026); FY2026 Annual Report (53 weeks to 31 Jan 2026): cash flow statement p.10519-10560, trading cash flow bridge p.2780-2788, FY2027 forecast p.2372-2376, shares in issue p.9661, ESOT holdings p.13458, NCI p.10511; kpis table for lease liabilities, lease principal, ESOT purchases, cash taxes, depreciation
data_sources.qualitative: NXT.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10); Q2 FY2027 trading statement 5 Aug 2026 (NXT.L_Quarterly_Q2-2026.txt) for the raised guidance and buyback ceiling

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026 statutory revenue, 53 weeks to 31 Jan 2026. The 53rd week (~1.9% of revenue, GBP24m PBT) is inside the base, so the FY2027 year-1 growth rate is the guided +6.6% Total Group sales growth re-based for the 53rd week (1.066/1.019 - 1 = +4.6%).
inputs.share_count_basis: Shares in circulation at 31 Jan 2026: 122,436,612 in issue less 5,504,760 held by the ESOT = 116.93m (FY2026 AR p.9661 and note p.13458). This is the basis management uses for EPS and for the buyback ERR test. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, and the ESOT's market purchases are the cash mechanism that keeps the circulating count flat. Buybacks since 31 Jan 2026 (1.51m shares by 24 Mar; GBP355m / ~2.8m shares by 5 Aug 2026) are deliberately NOT netted off, because the matching net-debt increase is not yet in a published balance sheet; the Jan 2026 share count and Jan 2026 net debt are the self-consistent pair.
inputs.net_debt_note: Bonds, bank loans and overdrafts less cash at 31 Jan 2026, EXCLUDING IFRS 16 lease liabilities of GBP999.8m (leases are charged as an operating cost in the flows -- treatment B). Company's own 'net debt excluding leases' is GBP713.4m (FY2026 AR p.14098). FY2027 guidance: net debt rises to ~GBP790m after GBP524m buybacks and GBP318m dividends.
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income on cash deposits was GBP11.0m in FY2026 but the company is a net borrower (net debt GBP713m), so no cash pile is being double-counted; left at 0 per the net-cash rule. NEXT Finance's ~GBP301m of customer interest income is operating revenue, not deposit interest, and stays in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 AR note p.11949: share-based payment expense equity-settled GBP43.6m (cash-settled GBP0.3m is already cash). CSV StockBasedComp 43.1. Next does not net-settle for tax (EquityAwardTaxes = 0); instead the ESOT buys shares in the market -- net ESOT purchases were GBP61.8m in FY2026 (GBP169.0m bought, GBP107.2m disposed/exercise proceeds). The P&L IFRS 2 charge is used as the house SBC cost; the ESOT cash outlay (5-yr avg ~GBP60m vs SBC ~GBP32m) is the cash cross-check and would add ~GBP1.50/share of cost if used instead.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 financing outflow: repurchase of own shares GBP131.4m plus GBP421.5m returned via the B Share Scheme and GBP286.5m ordinary dividends (total GBP839m). FY2027 allocation GBP524m, GBP355m spent by 5 Aug 2026 at avg GBP127.69; buybacks are subject to an 8% ERR test implying a GBP135 price ceiling, so at the current price the remaining GBP169m is expected to be returned as a special dividend. The flat count is being funded (repurchaser).
inputs.fx_note: Statements in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts model GBP per share to quote pence. No FX exposure in the conversion; parity check: 52-week range 11,695-16,175p brackets the quote.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T16:15:00Z (LSE regular close, Friday; Yahoo chart API)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP: 10-year gilt ~4.5%, UK ERP 5.0%, equity beta ~1.0 (Next vs FTSE 100) gives cost of equity ~9.5%; ex-lease net debt GBP713m at ~5% pre-tax / 3.75% post-tax against a ~GBP17bn market cap gives a ~96/4 weighting and a WACC of 9.0%. Leases are excluded from the capital structure because they are charged as an operating cost in the flows. The same 9.0% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality, Shein share-loss and Equal Pay risk are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B) -- leases as operating cost. Lease principal (GBP167.4m, 'Lease payments' in financing, FY2026 AR p.10548) plus lease interest paid (GBP56m, management's trading cash flow bridge p.2782; P&L lease interest GBP48.7m) are deducted inside adjusted EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path (3.24% of FY2026 revenue). Lease liabilities (GBP999.8m) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A for the cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation: GBP153m 'depreciation of assets and amortisation of software' (p.2375) against total D&A of GBP334.7m, so the lease is charged once. Check: FY2026 EBITDA 1,613.5 - SBC 43.1 - lease 223.4 - D&A 153 = 1,194 EBIT vs management's 'operating profit after lease interest' GBP1,187m.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: non-controlling interests (Reiss 25.7%, Joules, FatFace minorities) deducted at book value GBP118.0m (equity statement at 31 Jan 2026). FY2026 profit attributable to NCI was GBP9.2m; an earnings-based value (~15x) would be ~GBP138m, GBP0.17/share more -- immaterial. Flows are consolidated (100%) so the deduction is required.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 2: non-US operating company, consumer, cyclical, with material leases and a minority interest -- owner-fcf.md plus owner-fcf-adaptations.md sections a, b, c, f applied). Fresh build, no prior DCF and no memory entry. Owner FCF FY2026 = reported FCF 1,062.4 (statutory OCF 1,233.6 is pre-interest since interest paid sits in financing, less PP&E 135.4 and intangibles 35.8) - SBC 43.1 - lease principal 167.4 - lease interest 56.0 = 795.9 (11.5% of revenue). Year-1 cross-check: management's FY2027 forecast of GBP741m 'cash generation before investments and distributions' at GBP1,210m PBT, re-based to the raised GBP1,243m guidance (+GBP25m post-tax), with external interest (~GBP39m) and ESOT purchases (~GBP62m) added back and SBC (~GBP45m) charged, implies ~GBP820m of house owner FCF; the base component build gives ~GBP830m. Tax: UK 25% headline, guided ETR 25.0%, applied flat (FY2026 cash tax of GBP233m was timing-light vs a GBP288m charge, not a shelter). Working capital capture -10% of the revenue change: NEXT Finance receivables (~GBP1.3bn) and inventory exceed payables, so growth consumes cash; FY2025-26 averaged roughly -8 to -24% with 53rd-week noise. Horizon 10 years: capex steps up to GBP237m in FY2027 for the E3 warehouse (GBP307m over three years) and the capex/D&A gap does not normalise until ~year 6.

bear.narrative: FY2027 lands near guidance (H1 is in the bag) but FY2028-29 stall: the ZEOS and WOBL stock-availability one-offs annualise, International marketing ROI slides toward the GBP1.01 breakeven management warns of, Shein and Chinese marketplaces take UK online share from the LABEL aggregator as well as from ASOS/Boohoo, and a soft UK consumer deepens the store estate decline past -3% a year so lease and wage costs deleverage. The claimants win the Equal Pay appeal, adding a structural store wage cost. EBITDA margin compresses to 21%; the lease charge rises to 3.35% of revenue; E3 capex still has to be spent. Terminal growth 1.5%, exit capped at 13x.

base.narrative: FY2027 follows the raised guidance (Total Group sales +6.6%, PBT GBP1,243m, capex GBP237m, 25% tax). Growth then fades from 4% to 2.5% as International online (+14-19%) and LABEL/WOBL offset a -1.5% to -3% store estate and a flat NEXT Finance book. EBITDA margin edges from 23.4% to 23.8% as efficiency gains and online mix offset UK wage inflation; the lease charge drifts from 3.2% to 2.9% of revenue as the store estate shrinks in relative terms. Capex runs at 3.3-3.0% through the E3 warehouse programme and settles at 2.6% against D&A of 2.4%. Terminal growth 2.0%, exit capped at 15x owner FCF.

bull.narrative: The beat-and-raise pattern continues: H2 FY2027 sales beat the +5% guide as they did in Q2, International online compounds at 15-20% for several more years as marketing ROI holds above GBP1.75 per GBP1 and more aggregator deals follow ZEOS, WOBL and LABEL third-party brands keep adding GBP300-400m a year, and Total Platform signs further clients at ~23% ROCE. Online mix and fixed-cost leverage lift EBITDA margin to 25% while the lease charge falls to 2.6% of revenue. The Equal Pay appeal is exhausted in Next's favour. Terminal growth 2.5%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 20/50/30. Bear up to 20% because three independent, slow-moving headwinds are live at once -- structural store decline with new stores missing sales targets by ~12%, Shein taking UK online apparel share, and a possible further Equal Pay appeal -- and because UK wage/NI policy is a recurring cost shock; none threatens solvency (viability test withstands an 18% sales fall), which is why it is not higher. Bull down to 30% because the bull case needs International growth to persist through the ZEOS annualisation AND marketing ROI to hold AND margin to expand by 160bp, three things that must go right together, albeit at a company with a long record of beating its own guidance.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
